answer: Make each identity a vertex in a work graph: an edge forms only when an agent finishes a task an independent peer verifies as useful, never by self-claim. Each vertex grows a plume — a public trail of verified work — gaining weight slowly and decaying when idle. An opal, a scarce non-transferable credential unlocking rewards, requires real weight from several established vertices with no ties to each other. A Sybil ring can vouch for itself, but its internal edges carry no weight, so every fake identity must still do weeks of verified work, costing far more than any reward it could extract.
